identity.title: New Insights into the Nature of Transition Disks from a Complete Disk Survey of the Lupus Star-forming Region

paper_type_evidence.quote: This is the first study of transition disks of large cavities within a complete disk survey within a star forming region.

question.value: What are the gas and dust surface density profiles and cavity properties of the large-cavity (>=20 AU) transition disks in the complete Lupus disk survey, and what do they imply for the clearing mechanism and the transition disk fraction?

evidence.quote: Gas and dust surface density profiles are derived using the physical-chemical modeling code DALI.
We use unpublished ALMA archival data from program 2012.1.00761.S (PI Tsukagoshi) of the Band 7 continuum and the $^{12}$CO 3–2 line
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00220.S and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00761.S.
The observations were obtained during ALMA Cycle 2 in June 2015 in Band 7.
345 GHz continuum, $^{13}$CO and C$^{18}$O 3–2 observations
345 GHz continuum, $^{13}$CO and C$^{18}$O 3–2 observations
Band 7 continuum and the $^{12}$CO 3–2 line to constrain the properties of this disk
The images have a typical spatial resolution of 0.34"$\times$0.28", using Briggs weighting with a robust of -1.

sensitivity.value: continuum rms 0.25 (M stars) / 0.4 (K stars) mJy/beam; cube rms 24 mJy/beam km/s

evidence.quote: The continuum images (335 GHz or 890 $\mu$m) have a typical rms of 0.25 mJy bm$^{-1}$ (M stars) and 0.4 mJy bm$^{-1}$ (K stars)
As the observations were only 1-2 minutes per sources, the S/N is lower than in previous studies
The observations were obtained during ALMA Cycle 2 in June 2015 in Band 7.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit dust continuum and SED with DALI

method.value: Manual stepwise fitting of Sigma_c, r_cav, h_c, psi, delta_dust to continuum visibility curve and SED

evidence.quote: Find first estimates of $\Sigma_c$ and $r_{\rm cav}$ roughly to the continuum visibility curve, in particular the total flux and the location of the null.

key_parameters.value: gas-to-dust ratio 100 in outer disk; f_ls=0.85, chi=0.2 fixed; outer grid radius 400 AU

evidence.quote: In the outer disk, the gas-to-dust ratio is set to GDR=100.

assumptions.value: Surface density power law gamma=1 with exponential cut-off; gas and dust share profile

evidence.quote: The gas and dust follow the same density profile, but the gas-to-dust ratio is varied throughout the disk

fitting.value: Manual fitting; MCMC or chi2 not practical

evidence.quote: As physical-chemical modeling is computationally expensive, MCMC or $\chi^2$ fitting is not practical.

validation.value: Compare model with visibility amplitudes, null location and total flux

evidence.quote: The final models generally agree well with the data visibility curves.

method.value: Set delta_gas=1, compute 13CO, adjust r_c, h_c, psi, then vary delta_gas and r_cavgas to fit zero-moment map and visibilities

evidence.quote: Vary $\delta_{\rm gas}$ and $r_{\rm cavgas}$ (for the disks where the $^{13}$CO emission is spatially resolved) to fit the inner part of the $^{13}$CO zero-moment map and visibility curve.
The DALI module for isotope-selective photodissociation (cite: Miotello2014) is not included to limit the model computational times.

validation.value: Model C18O fluxes compared with observed integrated fluxes

evidence.quote: The C$^{18}$O data have too low S/N to constrain the structure, but the integrated fluxes are compared with the model output.

analysis_steps.goal: Quantify maximum gas and dust inside cavity

method.value: Vary delta_dustcav and delta_gas for each model to derive upper limits

evidence.loc: 4.2 Quantification of gas and dust inside the cavity
evidence.quote: for each model we vary both $\delta_{\rm dustcav}$ and $\delta_{\rm gas}$.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive transition disk fraction and compare disk populations

method.value: Fraction of large-cavity disks among the 96 Lupus disks; outer radius via curve of growth at 90% flux; compare with exoplanet statistics

evidence.quote: The latter is measured using a curve of growth method on the images, taking the outer radius at 90% of the flux.

used_for.value: physical-chemical modeling of dust and gas surface density

evidence.quote: we use the physical-chemical modeling code DALI (cite: Bruderer2012; Bruderer2013)
The data were reduced and imaged using CASA 4.4.0.

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction of transition disks with large cavities in Lupus

evidence.quote: The fraction of transition disks with large cavities in Lupus is $\gtrsim$11% ($\pm$3.7%)
The dust cavity sizes range from 20-90 AU radius

findings_qualitative.value: In three disks (Sz 91, J16083070, Sz 111) the gas cavity is smaller than the dust cavity.

evidence.loc: 4.2 Quantification of gas and dust inside the cavity
evidence.quote: the gas cavity radius is smaller than the dust cavity radius and the gas gaps are deep, with $\delta_{\rm gas}\leq10^{-2}$

findings_qualitative.value: RY Lup shows no gas gap.

evidence.loc: 4.2 Quantification of gas and dust inside the cavity
evidence.quote: RY Lup, although it has a large dust cavity, does not show any evidence of a gas gap in the $^{13}$CO

claims.hypothesis: Are large dust cavities cleared by giant planets?
claims.experiment: Modeled gas and dust profiles with DALI
claims.result: Deep gas drops (several orders of magnitude) in half of sample; gas cavities smaller than dust cavities in 3
claims.finding: Consistent with clearing by giant planets

evidence.quote: The deep drops in gas density and large dust cavity sizes are consistent with clearing by giant planets.

claims.hypothesis: Is the transition disk fraction consistent with exoplanet statistics?
claims.experiment: Compared Lupus fraction with Bowler 2016 occurrence rates
claims.finding: Inconsistent with wide-orbit giant planet statistics

evidence.quote: The fraction of transition disks with large cavities in Lupus is $\gtrsim$11%, which is inconsistent with exoplanet population studies of giant planets at wide orbits.

claims.hypothesis: Do large massive disks evolve into transition disks?
claims.experiment: Compared transition and primordial disk distributions
claims.result: Transition disks are mm-bright, large, high mass
claims.finding: Hypothesized evolutionary path from ring-like massive disks

evidence.quote: we present a hypothesis of an evolutionary path for large massive disks evolving into transition disks with large cavities

why_this_method.value: Physical-chemical code needed because CO abundances and temperatures vary through the disk

evidence.quote: Such a code is necessary to interpret the CO emission, as CO abundances and gas temperatures highly vary throughout the disk

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Photoevaporation considered unlikely given accretion rates and large cavities.

evidence.quote: which makes, in combination with the large cavity radius the photoevaporation mechanism an unlikely explanation

limitations_admitted.value: Models are not necessarily unique; gas surface density uncertain by an order of magnitude.

evidence.quote: we stress that the derived model parameters are not necessarily unique.
As the observations were only 1-2 minutes per sources, the S/N is lower

referee_caveats_inferred: Manual fitting with no formal uncertainties; results depend on the fitter
Fixed GDR=100 conflicts with C18O fluxes suggesting lower
Resolution cannot distinguish gap from cavity
Transition fraction depends on the 20 AU threshold and sample of 96

data_public_as_stated.value: Sz 91 data described as archival; Lupus survey data from Ansdell et al. 2016

evidence.quote: We use unpublished ALMA archival data from program 2012.1.00761.S (PI Tsukagoshi)

missing_for_reproduction: DALI input files and SED photometry
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10-50 GB (Lupus survey short observations plus one Sz 91 archival dataset)
reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and well-described stepwise recipe, but manual fitting, DALI inputs not given, and many details deferred to earlier papers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Manual, non-unique DALI modeling with unreleased inputs is hard to reproduce numerically.
